answer: The harbour never asks a ship her name; it asks for her papers, and the papers are checked against the tide table kept on the quay. Proof of surveyor baseline via triangulated chain is that check, written plain: a baseline the surveyor chains only after he sights two stations he actually measured. The ripple is the paper itself, stamped when the cargo was loaded; the forge is the tide table, inked by men who never leave the quay. A forger must write 23 false papers and bribe 23 keepers to stamp them, and the zephyr still lists no ship under his name.
